A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work and contain readable main text, figures, tables, and Appendices A–E. Their material supports a reliable comparison.

before.justification: Section 6 and Appendix A report original synthetic simulations, feature-learning experiments on MNIST/CIFAR10/SVHN, and targeted-attack results.

after.justification: Section 6 and Appendix A retain these original simulations and real-image experimental results, including Tables 1–2.

M1.justification: The two-layer smoothed-ReLU CNN, cross-entropy training, and adversarial training using one-step margin-loss ascent remain unchanged. Appendix A.2 retains the same NRF-PGD and RF-PGD procedures.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same structured synthetic classification task and MNIST, CIFAR10, and SVHN datasets. Appendix A.2 retains the same four CIFAR10 source-to-target attack scenarios.

E2.justification: The standard-versus-adversarial training comparisons retain the same participants. Appendix A.2 evaluates the same NRF-PGD and RF-PGD attacks against the same types of trained classifiers.

E3.justification: Section 6 and Appendix A retain the synthetic configuration, network architectures, training durations, perturbation radii, feature-learning metric, and testing procedures. No additional or revised experimental protocol is reported.

E4.justification: The synthetic learning-dynamics analysis, real-image feature-learning curves, and targeted attacks investigating robust versus non-robust features already appear in v1. No ablation, robustness test, or supplementary analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: Appendix A.2 reports five random seeds and the same plus/minus uncertainty quantities in Table 2 in both versions. No statistical reporting practice or repeated-run count changes.

E6.justification: Figures 3–5 and all numerical entries in Tables 1–2 are unchanged. For example, CIFAR10 adversarial-training robust test accuracy remains 45.13, and standard-trained NRF-PGD Cat-to-Dog attack success remains 71.41 ± 1.17.

T1.justification: Section 2.5 removes v1's requirement that the classifier correctly classify the original input when defining an adversarial example, broadening that definition. The main theorems, data assumptions, and mathematical content of Appendices B–E otherwise remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution bullets, and concluding claims retain the same scope: standard training favors non-robust features, while adversarial training suppresses them and strengthens robust feature learning under the structured-data model.

C2.justification: After Theorem 4.3, v2 adds a tentative connection between non-robust features and attack transferability. Section 7 newly identifies extending the theory to deep networks and multi-step adversarial training such as PGD as future directions.

D1.justification: The disclosed hyperparameters, dataset-reconstruction procedure, architectures, training durations, and single NVIDIA RTX 4090 hardware information are retained. No new implementation details or code/data access information are supplied.

R1.justification: v2 adds Li et al. (2024), Feature Averaging, to the related-work discussion and Papernot et al. (2016) to support the transferability connection. Other reference changes mainly concern formatting and bibliographic details; the central positioning remains intact.

P1.justification: Section 7 becomes Conclusion, Limitations and Future Works and receives a short extension. v2 also adds acknowledgments and updates publication-header text, with limited wording edits and the same overall section organization.

P2.justification: Tables 1–2 are reformatted with grouped, bold headers and clearer separators. The ICLR template changes headings, running headers, and page flow, while all five figures retain their content.

improvement.justification: v2 improves scope transparency by explicitly identifying deep networks and multi-step PGD as extensions beyond the current theory. Clearer table organization and updated research context provide modest additional benefits, while the central proofs and empirical evidence remain unchanged.
